note: Registered while walking Season in Part 1 of the conformance pass (2026-08-28). Every `expect` here is a selector observed on the page after the steps ran, captured by diffing the document's class set before and after — never guessed, because a state that cannot name its own subject reports a clean result for the DEFAULT view. The one-way strip is exercised in both directions: with the destroy capability and without it, because `Shell.canDestroy()` is the single authority and a strip that says owner-only while leaving a button live is the defect COMPANION §15.11 names.

states.note: preSettleMs because the manifest's search box does not exist until the realm's data has landed; typing into a selector that is not there yet is a step that silently does nothing, and `expect` is what turns that into a failure instead of a clean pass.

a draft is staged
states.note: A staged draft shows as its own rail below the divider, five lanes deep. `.srec-state.staged` was the first guess and is wrong: that class marks the record while you are EDITING the draft, not while one merely exists.

states.name: the page could not load
states.note: `.fail-a` is the way out. A failure state that names what happened and offers nothing is the pattern COMPANION §10.6 bans, so the action is the part worth asserting.

states.name: offline · the network banner
states.note: 🔴 THE FLAG IS `?fail=offline`, NOT `?offline=1`. async.js's own header and the conformance plan's flag list both name a bare `?offline=` parameter; stub.js has never read one. `?offline=1` renders the ordinary page, so a state registered under it would have walked the DEFAULT view and passed.

states.name: slow · the skeleton in the shape of the content
states.note: `slow` delays EVERY request including the session, so at 900ms the skeleton on screen says 'Signing in…' — the door's, not the realm's. preSettleMs past the session leaves the realm's own request in flight, which is the state this is for: it reads 'Loading…'.
